title: smart-routing-fallback-debug-notes-isaac
content:
Context:
Quick personal scratchpad capturing breadcrumbs from the 2026-02-12 regional failover incident (us-west -> eu-west fallback). Goal: capture commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses, and next steps for follow-up with SRE and routing owners. Not polished — notes for myself and on-call handoff.

High-level summary:
- Incident window: 2026-02-12 14:22:10 UTC -> 14:49:03 UTC (approx).
- Symptom: A subset of requests originating from hosted-api in us-west were routed to the regional fallback path but then faced immediate failures (504/upstream timeouts and 'fallback_failed: incompatible-model-variant').
- Impact: ~12% of production text-gen requests got errors or large latency spikes for ~25 minutes. Some customers on Dedicated saw route spillover.

Timeline / quick events (from logs + PagerDuty notes):
- 14:21:57 UTC - spikes in queue_depth downstream of rdw-router-service in us-west (queue_depth > 1200).
- 14:22:10 UTC - automatic smart-routing policy triggered regional-failover (policy: latency > 1200ms over 2m).
- 14:22:12 UTC - fallback routing decision sent: target region eu-west (model variant: gpt-medium-quant-v2).
- 14:22:13 UTC - many requests failed quickly with: 'fallback_failed: model-variant-mismatch' and gateway returned 502/504.
- 14:28:40 UTC - we disabled immediate regional failover for policy group 'low-latency' to stop cascading failures.
- 14:49:03 UTC - tear-down and routing normalized.

Commands & queries I ran during investigation:
- tail logs (router) to capture errors:
  sudo journalctl -u rdw-router -f --since "2026-02-12 14:20:00" | grep -E "fallback|fallback_failed|upstream|timeout|request_id"

- Check routing decision details (local dev tool):
  ./rdw-cli route-decision --request-id=9a7f2c1e --show-metrics
  output: decision=regional-failover target_region=eu-west target_model=gpt-medium-quant-v2 reason="latency_sla_breach"

- Example reproduced curl to hit the router with region hint (sanitized keys):
  curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'X-Client-Region: us-west' -H 'X-Request-ID: 9a7f2c1e' -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -> Response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
  Response body: {"error":"fallback_failed","message":"target model variant incompatible (quantization mismatch)"}

- Grepped proto mismatch logs on target region: (eu-west router logs)
  2026-02-12T14:22:13.104Z rdw-router[info] request_id=9a7f2c1e route=regional-failover target=eu-west variant=gpt-medium-quant-v2 result=fallback_reject reason="kv-cache-compat-failure"

- kube-level checks (eu-west):
  kubectl -n rdw get pods -o wide | grep model-serve
  kubectl logs model-serve-gpt-medium-quant-v2-0 -c grpc-proxy --since=1h | grep "compatibility"
  found: "model-serve: loaded quant profile v2; incoming request wants kv-format v1 -> compatibility=false"

Error snippets captured (raw):
- router: 2026-02-12T14:22:13.106Z ERROR request_id=9a7f2c1e fallback_failed: incompatible-model-variant kv_format_mismatch (expected=v2 actual=v1)
- gateway: 2026-02-12T14:22:13.109Z WARN upstream_http_error request_id=9a7f2c1e upstream_status=502 upstream_message="Bad Gateway"
- model-serve: 2026-02-12T14:22:13.115Z ERROR model-request: request_id=9a7f2c1e reject reason=kv_cache_header_missing

Observations / immediate hypotheses:
1) Model variant compatibility mismatch: router attempted to fail over to quant-v2 variant (eu-west) but some requests carried KV-cache header format v1 (from older sticky caches in us-west). The target model rejects v1 prefix + kv state, causing immediate fallback failure.
2) Stale routing policy config: There was a recent change in routing policy (PR #134) that expanded fallback targets to include gpt-medium-quant-v2 in eu-west for low-latency group. That PR did not include a compatibility matrix check.
3) Cache affinity issue: Clients that used sticky prefix caching in us-west have kv headers saved in v1 format; when the router simply routes them to eu-west without transforming or invalidating the kv header, the target rejects them.
4) Circuit breaker behavior: The router's fallback circuit (which should attempt alternate compatible variants) appears to short-circuit and return failure instead of trying the compatible plain fp32 variant in eu-west. Might be due to a bug in the variant compatibility check returning false positive.

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Locally emulate a request with v1 kv header and force regional failover:
  curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'X-Client-Region: us-west' -H 'X-KV-Format: v1' -H 'X-Request-ID: repro-req-001' -d '{"input":"test kv header"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?force_region=eu-west
  Expect: either router strips/invalidates header or routes to a compatible variant. Observed: immediate 502 with fallback_failed.

2) Run rdw-cli check-compat --source-kv=v1 --target-variant=gpt-medium-quant-v2 -> returns compatibility=false (as reproduced in logs).

Short-term mitigations already applied (by SRE during incident):
- Disabled regional-failover policy for group 'low-latency' at 14:28:40 UTC to stop additional failures.
- Rollback PR #134 on rdw-router (temporarily) to prevent selecting quant-v2 as fallback target for this policy group.

Longer-term fixes to consider (draft):
- Add compatibility matrix enforcement in router: do not select fallback target variants that are incompatible with the incoming KV cache/header. Enforce during decision stage (fast check).
- Add transform/strip mode: allow router to optionally strip kv headers when moving cross-region (toggle per-policy) to force cold start on target region when sticky kv is unsafe.
- Improve canary/testing: add an integration test that simulates kv-format mismatches across regions and ensures router won't pick incompatible variant.
- Telemetry improvement: emit structured metric 'fallback.reject.reason=compatibility' with target_variant tag, to make this class of failure SLO-detectable.
- Circuit breaker improvement: when primary fallback fails due to compatibility, attempt secondary compatible variant (fp32) instead of immediate client error.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who owns the compatibility matrix? (Guess: serving-runtime + applied-ml) -> Need application owner to add to model catalog and router config.
- Are we able to add on-the-fly kv header translation between v1 and v2? Risky; prefer stripping for safety.
- Confirm whether Dedicated customers were silently impacted due to spillover (check billing/telemetry).

Notes for handoff to SRE & router owners:
- Relevant PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rdw-router/pull/134 (expanded fallback targets).
- Jira: JIRA-INFR-982 (incident ticket).
- Confluence incident doc: CONFLUENCE-INC-3241 (initial postmortem draft).
- Repro request id used above: repro-req-001 (use for logs grep).

Next actions (me / short list):
- [ ] Sync with @Olivia Park and @Marcus Li tomorrow 10:00 to align on compatibility enforcement design.
- [ ] Draft a router-side patch that checks model-catalog compatibility before selecting fallback target (quick guardrail).
- [ ] Add metric emit for fallback.reject.reason and dashboard tile.
- [ ] Write small integration test in rdw-router that simulates cross-region kv header v1 -> quant-v2 mismatch.

Handy log grep commands (for follow-up):
- grep request_id across infra: sudo journalctl -u rdw-router --since "2026-02-12 14:20:00" | grep 9a7f2c1e
- check model-serve logs in eu-west: kubectl -n rdw logs -l app=model-serve -c frontend --since=2h | grep "kv_format"

Random notes / stray observations while debugging:
- Not all requests failed; requests without X-KV headers succeeded when routed. Pattern solidly points to kv header incompatibility.
- One curious line: router emitted a decision 'target_variant=gpt-medium-quant-v2' but later the decision history shows 'candidate_list=[gpt-medium-quant-v2,gpt-medium-fp32]'. The code path seemed to pick quant-v2 then abort without attempting the next candidate. Need to trace the decision loop.

If anyone reading this — please add any missing breadcrumbs here. Will convert to formal incident write-up once we collect root-cause and RCA owners.

-- Isaac
